decisions.reason: PDF62/printed60 confirms a roughly three-week interval after transplanting before tillering begins. Current agr-ricework-water-p3 gives the definition only. Keep this as a source-example interval, not a universal date or separate number-substitution question.

PDF62/printed60 states tillering continues roughly six weeks after it begins. Do not interpret six weeks as an interval measured from transplanting. Merge the timeline-reading goal with0184; no separate question capacity credit.

PDF62/printed60 describes about20stems from one seedling before tillering stops. Current stages-p2 concerns ineffective tillers only. Preserve the approximate, source-example status; do not turn20into a universal threshold, planting target or operational trigger.

PDF62/printed60 explicitly connects continued flooding, ineffective tillers, advancing soil reduction/harmful substances and worse root condition. Current water-p4 defines midseason drainage without this causal explanation. It may support an explanatory scope, coordinated with0198 rather than duplicated.

PDF66/printed64 shows transplanting-machine examples from2to8rows. Current field-p4 and mockagr-1-m02-q12 already cover what row count means. The range may be added to source-bound prose but cannot create a new independent question just by changing numbers.

PDF66/printed64 gives both root-vigor improvement and ground-bearing-strength improvement as purposes of drying the field. Current water-p4 omits both. Retain the distinct plant/ground purposes. Do not derive a blanket drainage date or universal stage prescription from this paragraph; its printed stage wording must stay source-bound or be separately reconciled before operational teaching. Coordinate root-vigor explanation with0188.

PDF66/printed64 includes deeper water among cultural weed-prevention examples alongside autumn/spring tillage and puddling. Current s30-rice-detail-p2 includes tillage/puddling only. Retain as a listed prevention example; no depth, duration or all-stage instruction is provided or inferred.

PDF67/printed65 lists rice blast and brown spot as two disease names. Current rice stages-p2 does not teach this distinction. Accept naming scope only: the photographed leaf-blast example is not a comparative image set for these two diseases and cannot certify visual diagnosis or two independent questions.

The packet uses the kanji穎花 as the term; retain readingえいか alongside it and avoid collapsing flower, panicle and grain into synonyms. Source names alone do not certify independent question capacity.
